newsitem.title: TAIWAN: E.Asia Oilseeds - China drought impact seen minor.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Oilseeds - China drought impact seen minor.

text.p: The impact of a drought on Chinese soybean production is believed to be minor and the prospects of a bumper crop this year remain good, traders said on Monday.
"Drought in (China's) northern areas will only have a minor impact on the corn and soybean," a trader for a U.S. commmodity trader in China said.
Regional traders had earlier expressed worries that a dry spell in the key province of Heilongjiang would hit China's soybean crop.
Market estimates last week pegged soybean output at 14-16 million tonnes, up from the 1996 figure of around 13 million tonnes.
Dealers said the weather between now and the end of July would be vital to soybean growth.
In another development, Japanese soybean importers reacted calmly to the U.S. Department of Agriculture's (USDA) supply-demand report released on Friday.
Japanese traders said they would be sidelined this week because the report was within their expectations.
"We've covered our soybean supplies from Brazil this summer," a local soybean trader said. "There's no urgent need to buy old crop of U.S. soybean at the moment."
While rising U.S. Gulf/Japan freight rates would cause some to fret, one dealer said that it "will be basically quiet this week."
